system.name: VisME and MVEB
system.one_liner: A universal multimodal embedding model trained for visual identity discrimination, with a benchmark (MVEB) of four identity meta-tasks over 28 datasets.

content.variant_note: three tiles: a qualitative comparison on one request, the four benchmark meta-tasks around a mascot, and a grouped bar chart of results
content.argues: Existing embedding models return the wrong person for an identity request while VisME returns the right one, and the new benchmark and its scores show the gap across four identity tasks.
content.subject: A user request with right and wrong retrieved photos, four identity meta-tasks with query and candidate images, and Precision@1 bars of four models.

lessons.what_to_learn: Combine three tiles in one Figure 1: one request over red-framed failures and green-framed successes of the same query, the benchmark as a dashed four-quadrant card around a mascot with its counts, and a grouped bar chart whose spans name the benchmark families; repeat the task names across tiles.
lessons.suits: Benchmark-plus-method papers in retrieval or embedding learning, where concrete baseline failures motivate the benchmark.

evidence: Caption: (a) qualitative comparison with existing UMEs, (b) four meta-tasks of MVEB over 28 datasets, (c) quantitative evaluation on MVEB and MMEB.
Introduction: visual identity discrimination is decomposed into recognition, re-identification, grounding and editing.
Introduction: current top embedding models often fail to distinguish the desired identity.

summary: The paper adds visual identity discrimination to universal multimodal embeddings, with a learning framework called VisME and a benchmark, MVEB, of four meta-tasks over 28 datasets. Figure 1 has three tiles. At top left a cartoon user asks for more photos of a famous person; a red-framed row of wrong photos from existing models, each with a cross, sits over a green-framed row from VisME, each with a tick. At top right a dashed frame with four quadrants, recognition, re-identification, grounding and editing, each with a prompt and query and candidate thumbnails, surrounds a bee mascot with the counts 4 and 28. Across the bottom a grouped bar chart shows Precision@1 of four models, with VisME highest.
